title: Repository Contract Parity
intent: Run one behavioral contract across memory and PostgreSQL repositories.
problem: Without one behavioral suite executes against memory and PostgreSQL adapters, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the repository contract parity contract.
context: This pattern addresses multiple persistence adapters implement one port; its concrete control is one behavioral suite executes against memory and PostgreSQL adapters.
forces: Correctness requires that adapter-visible outcomes remain equivalent
Operational pressure can cause: memory tests miss transaction behavior
solution: Implement one behavioral suite executes against memory and PostgreSQL adapters. Verify the anchored symbol `Base` with `test_upgrade_repository_contract_and_downgrade` before reuse.
invariants: database-specific constraints strengthen rather than alter contracts
failure_modes: SQL null or JSON semantics diverge
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `memory tests miss transaction behavior` and fails closed if the repository contract parity evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For repository contract parity, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to one behavioral suite executes against memory and PostgreSQL adapters.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: multiple persistence adapters implement one port
Do not apply when: only one storage engine will ever exist
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
applies_when: multiple persistence adapters implement one port
not_when: only one storage engine will ever exist
